title: fix(cuda-graph): address warmup regression with shape guards in capture/replay
author: Alyssa Cho
release_notes:
- Fix regression causing slow warmups during CUDA graph replay when shape guards are present
- Add deterministic capture path and additional unit tests
description: Context: recent CUDA graph capture/replay work added shape-guard insertion to ensure correctness across dynamic shapes, but a regression was introduced where redundant or unordered shape guards caused captures to diverge across similar requests. That divergence prevented graph reuse and triggered frequent re-captures during warmup, increasing P99 warmup latency and causing throughput regressions in continuous-batching workloads. Motivation: restore deterministic capture/replay behavior and bring warmup latency back in line with pre-regression numbers while keeping correctness guarantees for dynamic shapes. What this PR does: canonicalize shape guards during capture to produce a stable, order-insensitive representation; avoid inserting redundant guards for identical dimension constraints; preserve KV-cache tensor layout metadata across capture/replay so replays do not force expensive reallocation/permutes; add a lightweight heuristic to skip guard insertion for scalar/trivial-dim shapes that previously caused noise; improve capture metadata hashing so equivalent graphs with reordered guards map to the same cache key. Changes included (high level): - runtime/cuda/cuda_graph_manager.{cc,h}: add canonicalization utilities, stable hashing for capture keys, and API to attach layout-preservation hints. - runtime/scheduler/capture_replay.cpp: integrate canonicalization step before capture and update replay path to consult preserved layout metadata. - runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_store.cc: store kv-cache layout descriptors alongside tensors and avoid re-layout on replay. - tests/regressions/test_cuda_graph_shape_guard.cpp: added deterministic replay and warmup latency regression tests across a variety of sequence lengths and batch sizes. - docs/release-notes/2025-01-20.md: notes about regression fix and recommended operator versions. Checklist: - [x] Add canonicalization and stable hashing for capture keys - [x] Preserve KV-cache layout across replay - [x] Add unit + integration tests reproducing regression and validating fix - [x] Run perf canary and load test - [x] Update release notes with user-facing impact and mitigation steps Performance: In our perf canary (gpt-like base model, seq=1024, batch=8, continuous batching enabled) warmup P95 dropped from ~1.1s to ~150ms on a 4xA100 pool; graph reuse rate during ramp improved from ~35% to >95% on typical traffic traces. Unit evasion/AVX invariant tests added to prevent future accidental reorderings. Testing & validation: local unit and integration tests pass; CI initially surfaced a flaky test in capture replay ordering (fixed in a follow-up commit by adding deterministic sort); perf-canary tests run in infra and confirmed improvement; manual smoke on dedicated cluster validated no functional regressions for cached KV lookups. Related Linear tasks: ENG-1423 (investigate warmup regression), ENG-1425 (stabilize cuda graph capture keys). Related PRs: pr-18345, pr-18712 (earlier cuda-graph capture/replay work).
commits: canonicalize(shape-guards): stable ordering and deduplication during capture
fix(kv-cache): persist layout descriptors to avoid re-layout on replay
hashing: compute deterministic capture key insensitive to guard order
test(cuda-graph): add regression tests for warmup and deterministic replay
docs: release notes for cuda graph warmup regression fix
